about: The closed list of physics material ids (AST-05, setup-asset-pipeline design decision 6, physics review R3). Every collision shape's 'material' and every material slot's 'physics' must be an id of 'materials'; lib/meta.validate refuses anything else. New ids are added here with physics sign-off, never invented in a generator. The values are the physics engineer's to tune in phases 3 and 6.

fields.friction_static: mu_s of the drone's polymer parts on the dry material
fields.stiffness_n_per_m: contact compliance of the surface; absent means rigid
fields.damping_ratio: zeta of that compliance; present with stiffness_n_per_m
fields.edge_radius_m: the radius the fiber bends over at an arris; null means the shape's own radius (capsule, cylinder or sphere radius, or a snag's radius_m)
fields.label: where the numbers stand: pilot, measured, published, derived or assumed
fields.rationale: the source or the calculation, as recorded in the physics review

steel.label: assumed
steel.rationale: carried from surfaces-review §5 (polymer on dry mild steel, rolled or sawn edge)

sheet_metal.label: assumed
sheet_metal.rationale: carried: 0.5 mm corrugated sheet over a 1 m purlin span; its half-thickness edge cuts the fiber

timber.label: assumed
timber.rationale: carried; a batten asset may override with ≈ 1e5 N/m

masonry.label: assumed
masonry.rationale: carried: brick, block, render; a worn arris

concrete.label: assumed
concrete.rationale: plastic feet on cast concrete sit in the published 0.5–0.7 band; a cast arris. Broken edges and rebar are 'edge' snags with their own radius

glass.label: assumed
glass.rationale: plastic on glass; a broken pane edge is a blade. Breakability is a later material property (review P3-6)

cable.label: assumed
cable.rationale: carried; rigid locally, the span compliance T = w·L²/(8·sag) comes from the wire geometry; the edge radius is the wire's own

foliage.label: derived
foliage.rationale: a 20 mm green branch at 1 m, E ≈ 10 GPa (published 8–12 GPa for green wood), I = πd⁴/64 = 7.85e-9 m⁴, k = 3EI/L³ ≈ 236 N/m; ζ assumed for a leafy branch; the edge radius is the branch's own
